notes:
Compact CRM notes and call fragments.
- Product: mid-market e‑commerce platform providing post-purchase customer care for 4000+ merchants.
- Primary workload: chat-based support agent that (a) answers shipment/returns queries, (b) triggers carrier lookups via tool-calls, (c) synthesizes return labels.
- Performance targets: aiming for p95 end-to-end <= 250ms for text streaming responses on common paths; p95 for tool-call roundtrip <= 400ms. Wants streaming to start sending tokens asap (progressive UI) — major UX ask.
- Throughput: baseline 120 RPS during weekdays, peak simulation target ~380 RPS for promos/holidays; concurrent chat windows approx 8k active sessions during peak.
- Reliability: require predictable degradation — fallback to smaller curated model variant + graceful partial responses when capacity constrained.
- Security: must support SSO/SAML for internal admin console, audit logs for customer interactions, KMS integration for encryption keys, and option to restrict EU customer data residency.
- Commercial: evaluation of Hosted API first to move quickly; if Hosted meets latency & predictable cost, customer will consider Dedicated (6-month commit) for predictable unit cost and isolation.
- Quote from Head of Product: "We can't have 1s p95 spikes during Black Friday — our CSAT drops immediately."
- Tech constraints: carrier tool-call needs stable outbound IPs for carrier allowlists; vendor must support webhooks and long-poll streaming.
- Internal champions: Head of Product (Cait Nguyen), Platform Lead (Diego Morales).
- Pricing sensitivity: mid-market procurement — wants a blended rate for high-volume bursts, asks for committed discount tiers.
- Artifacts: sample transcript + synthetic receipts uploaded to Drive, security questionnaire in drive link above.
- Recommended Redwood angle: showcase streaming + function calling example using customer's shipment-tracker tool, run synthetic holiday spike during Hosted API POC, provide quantized cost vs latency analysis and Dedicated pricing for predictable monthlies.
